sources.snippet: Chandrayaan-3 is a follow-on mission to Chandrayaan-2 to demonstrate end-to-end capability in safe landing and roving on the lunar surface. It consists of Lander and Rover configuration.

sources.title: Chandrayaan-3 - ISSDC
sources.snippet: Chandrayaan-3 is a follow-on mission to Chandrayaan-2 to demonstrate end-to-end capability in safe landing and roving on the lunar surface. It consisted of a Lander, Rover and Propulsion module to carry the landing module till 100km lunar orbit.

sources.title: Chandrayaan-3 - Wikipedia
sources.snippet: Chandrayaan-3 (CHUN-drə-YAHN / ˌtʃʌndrəˈjɑːn /) is the third mission in the Chandrayaan programme, a series of lunar-exploration missions developed by ISRO. The mission consists of Vikram, a lunar lander, and Pragyan, a lunar rover, as replacements for the equivalents on Chandrayaan-2, which had crashed on landing in 2019.

sources.title: Chandrayaan programme - Wikipedia
sources.snippet: The Chandrayaan programme (/ ˌtʃʌndrəˈjɑːn / CHUN-drə-YAHN) (Sanskrit: Candra 'Moon', Yāna 'Craft, Vehicle', pronunciation ⓘ) [4][5] is an ongoing series of outer space missions by ISRO for the exploration of the Moon. answer: Scientists from NRSC/ISRO estimate that about 2.06 tonnes of lunar epiregolith were ejected and displaced over an area of 108.4 m2 around the landing site [1]. LIBS confirmed the presence of sulphur on the lunar surface through unambiguous in-situ measurements [1]. APXS detected the presence of minor elements near the landing site [1]. ChaSTE provided the first observations from the payload onboard the Vikram Lander [1]. RAMBHA-LP measured near-surface plasma content around the landing site [1].
